raw: {"subevents":[{"id":"0","subevent":"A mortar attack in northern Faryab province killed at least four civilians and wounded 10 others on Thursday morning."},{"id":"1","subevent":"The attack happened around 11:00am local time when a mortar round landed in a market in Shareen Tagab district."},{"id":"2","subevent":"Abdul Karim Yourish, spokesman for the provincial police chief, said the mortar was fired by the Taliban to target security forces."},{"id":"3","subevent":"Yourish said all the victims were civilians who were at the market to shop."},{"id":"4","subevent":"The Taliban has not commented on the attack."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "Tunisia Youth Impact is using Voticook cooking contests, in which participants vote for the winner, to encourage rural women to vote and raise awareness of democratic participation."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "On Saturday, October 12, in the rural town of Echamine, the country is preparing for the second round of the presidential election between Nabil Karoui and Kais Saied, with first-round turnout at 48.98%."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "Wafa Tarhouni, president of the association, explains that the contest is a 'practice vote' where women compete through their dishes to be elected by the diners."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "Volunteers from Tunisia Youth Impact replicate real-life voting conditions, including electoral lists, voting booths, and sealed ballot boxes, with the ink replaced by a water-and-shampoo mixture."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "The contest takes place in the concrete courtyard of Hinda Jlass's half-built home, where the mother of four is preparing her couscous."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "Hinda Jlass says the event is a way of getting together with other women and that the essential thing is to participate; she plans to vote on Sunday, only the second time in her life."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "At noon, seven women from the village, including Hinda, compete by presenting dishes such as couscous, macaroni, rice, and salads to around fifty electors, with each competitor describing her dish."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "The electors taste the dishes and vote using the same procedure as in the presidential election, with volunteers guiding them to avoid invalid votes."}, {"id": "8", "subevent": "Members of the Tunisian election authority ISIE and EU election observer Stefan Ziegler are present, with Ziegler saying the event is original and good for Tunisian democracy."}, {"id": "9", "subevent": "After the voting, volunteers point out mistakes that could invalidate a vote, such as a signature instead of a cross."}, {"id": "10", "subevent": "Najwa Jlass, Hinda's sister, wins the contest and says she is happy to win but happier to see the community come together, adding that she will vote 'for real' the next day."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "Crime evolves with society, from opportunistic individual violations to a differentiated crime structure."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "Present-day organized crime is flexible, as exemplified by the Sicilian Cosa Nostra adapting to a changing economy."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "Cosa Nostra's wealth acquisition shifted from land to real property and businesses."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "Organized crime has become networks and alliances across borders, with links to legitimate institutions."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "Narcotics trafficking illustrates the intertwined crimes and corruption of officials, with proceeds laundered into the legal economy."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "Organized crime seeks a power monopoly and uses any means without concern for the rights of others."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "Common criminality and organized crime intersect, but organized crime is defined by continuity, hierarchy, and complex operations."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "Organized crime develops a mythology of invincibility that affiliates use to intimidate."}, {"id": "8", "subevent": "The reputation of organized crime affects mafiosi self-image, and a mafia 'hit' signals inner conflict."}, {"id": "9", "subevent": "Defining organized crime is difficult, but informants' confessions have provided documentation."}, {"id": "10", "subevent": "Nigerian criminal groups are flexible, family-based, with three types of structures, and are considered the most pervasive globally per the DOJ."}, {"id": "11", "subevent": "Nigerian scams and frauds caused hundreds of millions in losses in 1999, and in 1997 Boston authorities arrested check thieves who stole over $2 billion."}]}
